answer: Attention-anchor registration requires each identity to hold a public cedar log of sustained, time-stamped work on prior tasks before it can post new ones. The wharf rule enforces that an identity's posting rights scale only with demonstrated continuous engagement, measured as idle gaps below a threshold across many epochs. An attacker must therefore operate each fake identity through real, spaced activity for weeks, paying the opportunity cost of maintaining distinct persistent attention streams rather than spinning up cheap parallel accounts.
